assists.title: Card title in first-run setup: driving aids (traction control, ABS, racing line, automatic gears).
car.car: Card title in first-run setup: pick the car to drive.
car.livery: Card title: the car's paint scheme.
car.camera: Card title: the view the car starts in (cockpit, chase and so on).
device.keyboardDetail: Under the Keyboard tile. WASD = the W, A, S and D keys; keep it as is.
device.wheel: Tile: drive with a steering wheel and pedals.
device.wheelDetail: Under the Wheel tile. 1:1 = the car's steering turns exactly as far as the wheel in your hands.
device.touch: Tile on phones and tablets: drive with on-screen controls.
device.tilt: Tile on phones and tablets: steer by tilting the device.
device.tiles: Screen-reader name of the group of input device tiles.
device.connected: Small badge on the device tile whose controller or wheel is plugged in.
connectedDevices.title: Card title: every controller and wheel the browser can see.
connectedDevices.wheel: Badge before a connected device's name: it is a steering wheel.
connectedDevices.controller: Badge before a connected device's name: it is a gamepad.
connectedDevices.axesButtons: How many axes (sticks, pedals) and buttons a connected device reports. Add the plural forms your language needs.
connectedDevices.buttonMap: Button: shows a drawing of the controller with what every button does.
connectedDevices.hideMap: Button: hides the controller drawing again.
inputCheck.title: Card title: live bars showing what the game reads from the controller.
inputCheck.connected: Badge before the controller's name: it is plugged in and working.
inputCheck.steer: Label of a live bar (narrow, about 70 px): steering input.
inputCheck.throttle: Label of a live bar (narrow): the accelerator.
steeringFeel.title: Card title: how the controller steers, and its rumble.
steeringFeel.feel: Setting: how quick and how sharp the controller's steering is.
steeringFeel.testVibration: Row: run a short rumble test on the controller.
steeringFeel.test: Button that plays a short rumble.
padButtons.title: Card title: which controller button does what.
padButtons.descriptionCustom: Shown when the pedals are on neither the triggers nor the right stick.
padButtons.noGearUp: Gear up and Gear down are the names of two actions in the list below; use the same words as those actions.
padButtons.noGearDown: Gear up and Gear down are the names of two actions in the list below; use the same words as those actions.
padButtons.noGears: Gear up and Gear down are the names of two actions in the list below; use the same words as those actions.
padButtons.layout: Setting: ready-made button layouts (GT style and others).
padButtons.customLayout: Shown under the layouts when the buttons match none of them.
padButtons.layoutStickPedals: Under a layout tile. {up}, {down}: the gear-shift buttons' names, such as R2 and L2; keep them as they are.
padButtons.layoutTriggerPedals: Under a layout tile. {up}, {down}, {boost}: button names, such as RB, LB and R3; keep them as they are.
padButtons.stickClick: {button}: a stick's click button, such as R3. {action}: the action on it, already translated (e.g. Boost).
padButtons.pedals: Setting: where the throttle and brake are on the controller.
padButtons.triggers: Choice: the pedals are on the two triggers.
padButtons.triggersDetail: {throttle}, {brake}: trigger names such as RT and LT; keep them as they are.
padButtons.rightStick: Choice: the pedals are on the right stick.
padButtons.rightStickDetail: {throttle}, {brake}: trigger names such as RT and LT; keep them as they are.
padButtons.pressFor: Screen-reader label while waiting for a button. {action}: the action's name, already translated.
padButtons.boundAria: Screen-reader label of a binding button. {action}: the action, already translated. {button}: a button name such as RB.
padButtons.unboundAria: Screen-reader label of a binding button with no button set. {action}: the action, already translated.
padButtons.pressButton: On the binding button while it waits for a controller button.
padButtons.add: On an empty binding slot: press it to bind a button.
padButtons.clutch: Row: the clutch pedal, bound to a button.
padButtons.clutchHintSet: Rev on the spot = raise the engine speed while stopped; slip it off the line = let the clutch out gradually at the start.
padButtons.clutchAria: Screen-reader label. {source}: where the clutch is read, already translated (a button name or e.g. 'right stick down').
padButtons.refused: Shown when the pressed button is already a pedal. {button}: a button name such as RT; {pedal}: which pedal.
padButtons.refusedTriggers: Shown when the pressed button is already a pedal. {button}: a button name such as RT; {pedal}: which pedal.
padButtons.capturing: Esc is the key name; keep it. {seconds}: a number of seconds; s = seconds.
padButtons.hint: A slot is one of the binding buttons in the list. Gear up and Gear down are action names in the list.
padButtons.buttonMap: Button: shows a drawing of the controller with what every button does.
padButtons.hideMap: Button: hides the controller drawing again.
fineTuning.title: Card title: advanced controller settings (dead zones, curves).
tuning.stickResponse: Title of a small graph: how stick movement turns into steering.
tuning.pedalTrigger: Label above a live bar: the pedal is read from a trigger. {pedal}: Throttle, Brake or Clutch, already translated.
tuning.pedalSource: Label above a live bar. {pedal}: Throttle, Brake or Clutch, already translated. {source}: where the pedal is read, already translated (e.g. 'right stick up').
tuning.pedalReadout: Live readout: how far the pedal is pressed (in) and what the game uses after the curve (out). {raw}, {shaped}: 0 to 100.
assistCurve.title: Title of a small graph: how far the steering assist countersteers as the car's rear slides.
assistCurve.summaryFullLock: Beside the graph. {grip}: a percentage. Full lock = the steering turned as far as it goes.
assistCurve.summaryCap: Beside the graph. {grip}: a percentage. {cap}: the most the assist steers, in degrees.
assistCurve.slide: Axis label on the graph, drawn very small. {deg}: the rear's slide angle in degrees.
padMap.controller: Screen-reader name of the drawing of a controller.
padMap.steer: Beside the left stick in the controller drawing: it steers.
padMap.mfdDial: Beside the D-pad's left / right: switches the MFD dial (MFD = the car's multi-function display; keep the abbreviation).
padMap.mfdValue: Beside the D-pad's up / down: changes the selected MFD dial's value.
padMap.notUsed: Beside a controller button that has no action.
padMap.axisPedal: Beside a stick in the controller drawing: which pedal it works and in which direction.
padMap.axisPedals: Beside a stick: two pedals on it, e.g. 'Throttle up, brake down'.
keyBindings.title: Card title: which keyboard key does what.
keyBindings.resetWhat: Goes into the reset question 'Resets {what} to defaults.'
keyBindings.reserved: {key}: a key's name as printed on the keyboard; keep it as it is.
keyBindings.moved: Shown after a key is taken from another action. {key}: key name. {action}: the action it was on, already translated.
keyBindings.pressKey: On the binding button while it waits for a key.
keyBindings.pressKeyFor: Screen-reader label. {action}: the action's name, already translated.
keyBindings.boundAria: Screen-reader label of a key slot. {action}: the action, already translated. {key}: key name.
keyBindings.unbind: Screen-reader label of the small × button next to a key. {key}: key name. {action}: already translated.
keyBindings.addFor: Screen-reader label of an empty slot. {action}: already translated.
keyBindings.add: On an empty key slot: press it to add a key.
keyBindings.capturing: Esc is the key name; keep it. {seconds}: a number of seconds; s = seconds.
keyBindings.escPauses: Esc is the key name; keep it.
fixedKeys.title: Card title: keys that can't be rebound.
fixedKeys.pause: An action in the fixed keys list: open the pause menu.
fixedKeys.moveView: Hold Alt and press the arrow keys to move the camera inside the car (cockpit or dash view).
fixedKeys.mfdDials: MFD = the car's multi-function display; keep the abbreviation.
fixedKeys.boostChat: Typing / in the chat starts a command; here, the boost command.
fixedKeys.arrows: Drawn as a key cap: the arrow keys. Keep it very short.
keyboard.mouse: Card title: steering with the mouse.
keyboard.feel: Card title: how quickly keyboard steering and pedals respond.
dualSense.needsAdaptiveTriggers: Why a setting is greyed out. 'Adaptive triggers' is the name of the setting above it; use the same words.
dualSense.adaptiveTriggers: Setting: the DualSense's motorised triggers push back and vibrate.
dualSense.adaptiveTriggersHint: L2 and R2 are button names; keep them. ABS = anti-lock brakes; keep it. Lock-ups = wheels locking under braking.
dualSense.triggerStiffness: Setting: how hard the adaptive triggers push back.
dualSense.rumbleStrength: Setting: how strong the controller's rumble is.
dualSense.hapticStrength: Setting: how strong the HD haptics vibration is.
dualSense.engineVibration: Setting: the controller vibrates with the engine.
dualSense.lightbar: Setting: what the controller's coloured light bar shows.
dualSense.lightbarHint: Explains the Revs choice: the light shows engine speed. The shift point = the moment to change up a gear.
dualSense.lightbarRevs: Choice: the light shows the engine speed (revs).
dualSense.lightbarDriver: Choice: the light shows the player's own colour.
dualSense.revLights: Setting: the controller's small LEDs show the engine speed like a race car's shift lights.
dualSense.revLightsHint: Player LEDs = the row of small lights under the touchpad; mic LED = the light on the mute button.
dualSense.description: WebHID = the browser feature used to talk to the controller; keep it. USB HD haptics = fine vibration over a USB cable.
dualSense.pair: Row: connect the controller to the page.
dualSense.connect: Button: pair the DualSense with the page (the browser then asks which device).
dualSense.padLine: {name}: the controller's name. {transport}: USB or Bluetooth.
dualSense.padLineBattery: {name}: the controller's name. {transport}: USB or Bluetooth. {battery}: battery charge, 0 to 100.
dualSense.padLineCharging: {name}: the controller's name. {transport}: USB or Bluetooth. {battery}: battery charge, 0 to 100.
dualSense.hdHaptics: Setting: fine, sound-driven vibration (HD = high definition).
dualSense.testTriggers: Row: a short test of the adaptive triggers.
dualSense.testTriggersHint: L2 and R2 are button names; keep them.
dualSense.testHaptics: Row: a short vibration test through the HD haptics.
dualSense.testGripsHint: The controller's left and right handles vibrate in turn.
dualSense.test: Button that plays a short test.
gyro.title: Card title: steering by turning the controller (motion sensor).
gyro.description: WebHID = the browser feature used; keep it.
gyro.needsGyro: Why a setting is greyed out. 'Gyro steering' is the name of the setting above; use the same words.
gyro.lock: Setting: how far the controller is turned for the steering to reach full lock.
gyro.sensitivity: Setting: how strongly small turns steer.
gyro.linear: Value of the Sensitivity slider at its middle: steering follows the tilt one to one.
gyro.calmer: Value of the Sensitivity slider below the middle. {value}: a number such as 0.80.
gyro.sharper: Value of the Sensitivity slider above the middle. {value}: a number such as 1.20.
gyro.needsChrome: Why the setting is greyed out. WebHID = the browser feature; keep it.
gyro.padLine: {name}: the controller's name. {transport}: USB or Bluetooth.
gyro.tilt: Label of a live bar (narrow): how far the controller is turned.
gyro.noMotion: Shown beside the live bar while the controller sends no motion.
gyro.recentre: Row: set the controller's current position as straight ahead.
gyro.recentreButton: Button: set the current position as straight ahead.
calibration.steer.rest: Continue is the button below this text; use the same word.
calibration.throttle.rest: Continue is the button below this text; use the same word.
calibration.brake.rest: Continue is the button below this text; use the same word.
calibration.clutch.rest: Continue is the button below this text; use the same word.
calibration.continue: Button: go on to the next calibration step.
wheel.title: Card title: the steering wheel (the device you hold), not a car's road wheel.
wheel.noWheel: Card description while no wheel is connected.
wheel.needsWheel: Why a row is greyed out while no wheel is connected.
wheel.type: Setting: the kind of wheel base.
wheel.directDrive: Wheel type: the motor turns the wheel directly (no belts or gears).
wheel.directDriveDetail: Raw and unfiltered = the steering signal is used as it is.
wheel.beltGear: Wheel type: the motor turns the wheel through a belt or gears.
wheel.allAxes: Row: calibrate the steering and pedals one after another.
wheel.calibrateAll: Button: calibrate steering, throttle and brake one after another.
wheel.steeringMeter: Label of a live bar (narrow, about 60 px): the wheel's angle.
wheel.axisBound: {device}: the wheel's name. {axis}: the number of the axis it is read from.
wheel.calibrating: On the calibrate button while calibration is running.
wheel.calibrate: Button: measure this axis (steering or a pedal).
wheel.rotation: Setting: how far the wheel turns lock to lock, in degrees.
wheel.rotationHint: Wheel driver = the wheel maker's software. 1:1 = the car's steering turns exactly as far as the wheel. {f1}, {gt3}, {road}: degrees.
wheel.rotationCustom: Choice beside 540°, 900° and so on: set your own rotation.
wheel.customRotation: Slider row: the wheel's rotation in degrees, set by hand.
wheel.steeringFilters: Card title: steering lock per car class and smoothing filters.
wheel.steerLock: Setting row. {cars}: a car class such as 'Formula cars', or a car's name.
wheel.steerLockHint: Full lock = the steering turned as far as it goes. The rim = the wheel you hold.
wheel.steerLockReal: Slider value at its top: the real car's steering lock. {deg}: degrees.
wheel.lockClass.formula: Car class: single-seater formula cars (F1 style).
wheel.lockClass.prototypes: Car class: sports prototypes (closed-wheel endurance racers).
wheel.lockClass.lmdh: Car class: an LMDh endurance prototype. LMDh is a category name; keep it.
wheel.lockClass.groupA: Car class: 1990s Group A touring cars. Group A is a category name.
wheel.lockClass.group4: Car class: Group 4 racing car of the BMW M1 Procar series. Procar is a name; keep it.
pedals.title: Card title: the wheel set's foot pedals.
pedals.throttleMeter: Label of a live bar (narrow, about 60 px).
pedals.brakeMeter: Label of a live bar (narrow, about 60 px).
pedals.clutchMeter: Label of a live bar (narrow, about 60 px).
pedals.clutchOptional: Shown under Clutch while no clutch pedal is calibrated.
wheelButtons.title: Card title: which wheel button does what.
wheelButtons.description: Gear paddles = the shift paddles behind the wheel. Neutral = no gear.
wheelButtons.resetWhat: Goes into the reset question 'Resets {what} to defaults.'
wheelButtons.pressFor: Screen-reader label while waiting for a button. {action}: already translated.
wheelButtons.boundAria: Screen-reader label. {action}: already translated. {button}: the button's number.
wheelButtons.bound: On a binding button: the wheel button's number. Btn = button; keep it short.
wheelButtons.add: On an empty binding slot: press it to bind a button.
wheelButtons.capturing: Esc is the key name; keep it. {seconds}: a number of seconds; s = seconds.
wheelButtons.moved: Shown after a button is taken from another action. Btn = button. {button}: its number. {action}: already translated.
bridge.takenOver: Status badge: another browser tab now drives the wheel's force feedback.
bridge.off: Status badge: the force feedback bridge program isn't running. The bridge = a small helper program on the PC.
bridge.offLine: Keep the <cmd></cmd> tags around {command}; {command} is a terminal command and stays as it is.
bridge.remoteOrigin: Keep the <cmd></cmd> tags around {command}; {command} is a setting typed in a terminal and stays as it is.
bridge.looking: Status badge: searching for the bridge program.
bridge.bridge: Status badge: the bridge program is running and reports something (an error or waiting).
bridge.connected: Status badge: force feedback works through the bridge.
browserFfb.connected: Status badge: the browser drives the wheel's force feedback.
browserFfb.connectingLine: Status line while the browser connects to a wheel whose name isn't known yet.
browserFfb.stopped: Status badge: the browser's force feedback stopped with an error.
browserFfb.stoppedLine: {reason}: what went wrong (may stay in English). The bridge = a helper program on the PC.
browserFfb.stoppedDevice: {device}: the wheel's name. {reason}: what went wrong (may stay in English).
browserFfb.notPaired: Status badge: no wheel has been picked in the browser yet.
browserFfb.notPairedLine: Connect wheel is the button below; use the same words.
browserFfb.connect: Button: pick the wheel in the browser's device list.
diagnostics.copy: Button: copies technical details for a bug report.
diagnostics.copied: On the button for a moment after copying.
diagnostics.text: Screen-reader name of the box holding the technical details.
supportedWheels.title: Card title: a list of wheels and how well force feedback works on each.
supportedWheels.description: {summary}: which wheels have been tested, one or more sentences (may stay in English).
supportedWheels.browser: Badge in the wheel list. {level}: Tested, Expected, Unknown or No, already translated. Browser = force feedback straight from the browser.
supportedWheels.bridge: Badge in the wheel list. {level}: already translated. Bridge = force feedback through the helper program.
forces.title: Card title: force feedback (the wheel pushing back).
forces.needsFfb: Why a setting is greyed out: force feedback is switched off.
forces.invert: Setting: reverses the direction of the force feedback.
forces.invertHint: Test is the button in the row below; use the same word.
forces.testDirection: Row: a short test that pulls the wheel.
forces.connection: Card title: how the force feedback reaches the wheel (browser or bridge program).
forces.browserConnection: Setting: the browser drives the wheel's force feedback directly.
forces.browserConnectionHint: The bridge = a small helper program on the PC.
forces.effects: Card title: force feedback effects (kerbs, road feel and so on).
forces.effectsDescription: Centring spring = a setting in the wheel maker's software that pulls the wheel to the middle.
forces.fineTuning: Card title: advanced force feedback settings.
perCar.label: Row: cars that have their own force feedback strength.
perCar.none: Shown when no car has its own strength.
perCar.hint: {strength}, {minForce}: percentages. Strength and Minimum force are the names of two settings above; use the same words.
perCar.hintThisCar: {strength}, {minForce}: percentages. Strength and Minimum force are the names of two settings above; use the same words.
perCar.clear: Button: removes this car's own strength.
perCar.clearAll: Button: removes every car's own strength.
